tasks.short: Return dictated reports for physician review and record inclusion

steps.what: Verify the dictated report, patient identity and reviewing physician
Prepare the printed or electronic review packet with patient and report references
Approve the completed review packet and named physician destination
outputs: approved review packet v1 with physician destination

steps.what: Return the approved packet to the physician's review queue
inputs: approved review packet v1 with physician destination
outputs: packet v1 delivered for physician review

steps.what: Review the returned report and specify required clinical corrections
inputs: packet v1 delivered for physician review

steps.what: Apply the physician's corrections and prepare the final report for signature
Verify the corrected final report and authorize its signed record version
Commit the physician-authorized signed report to the current patient record
outputs: signed report v2 included in the patient record

tasks.design: Configure review-packet assembly and gated queue delivery inside {OTHER}, the transcription and patient-record system. Preserve physician review, transcriptionist correction and final physician authorization before the signed report's separate record commit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparing and returning review copies can involve manual packet handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native electronic review queues can replace supported packet preparation and return actions.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve clinical corrections and ensure the signed version is the corrected final report.
tasks.human_edge: Transcriptionist verifies routing; physician accepts clinical meaning.

ambition.what: Reduce review-copy handling while preserving clinical sign-off.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-6; clinical record permissions and applicable staff consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: electronic report review queues can route a version to a physician and preserve correction and signature stages.

assumptions: Boundary starts with an existing dictated report and ends with its signed record inclusion; it includes correction handling but not initial transcription. Physician review is unchanged other-role labour, excluded from focal savings.

Existing report producers provide report ID/version, patient/encounter ID and physician ID; s1 checks them. Missing identifiers require manual verification. s5 supplies actual correction instructions and s6 applies them; planned review status cannot stand in for a signature.

Native review queues come first. Central requires actual packet preparation and return handling today; it removes 70% of preparation and the distinct queue-send action. No shorter correction or physician review is claimed.

Same-record final commit is effectively zero; minimum 1 is retained. Packet approval follows packet creation; final signature authorization follows all corrections. Any edit voids its relevant approval.
Provisional total shares=100; focal B=80, R=56, gross=30%; focal upkeep=1 per 100 focal baseline hours; net=29%. Shares do not follow means priors.
unknowns: Actual packet preparation and return time
research_questions: Trace reports through initial return, correction and final signature, counting all actors separately.

already_counted.description: Verify final review packet and destination

incremental.description: Audit review routing and version-status failures

approvals.approved_version: approved review packet v1 with physician destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: native review routing already covers the work. High: 30 focal gross points require seven extra focal hours of routing exceptions plus one upkeep hour, leaving 22; physician time is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Produce medical and administrative materials from supplied sources

steps.what: Identify the required material type and verify supplied dictation, data and instructions
inputs: existing practitioner dictation or source material

steps.what: Transcribe or draft the medical report, correspondence or administrative material from supplied sources

loop.purpose: Convert supplied dictation or narrative into the requested material
loop.input: Verified dictation/source text and document-type requirements
loop.output: Source-linked draft preserving uncertainty and marking unclear passages
loop.check: Transcriptionist compares names, medical terms, negation, chronology, omissions and intended meaning against audio/text; numbers are copied from structured sources
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unclear content returns for practitioner clarification
loop.why_not_simpler: Speech recognition and free-text transcription require interpretation; templates handle fixed structure and numeric tables first

steps.what: Format the requested material and insert source-supplied references or statistical tables
Verify source fidelity, correct errors and approve the production copy
Save the approved production copy in its current workspace
outputs: saved production copy v1 for subsequent clinical review

tasks.design: Use bounded transcription in {OTHER} and native {DOCS} templates to produce the requested material from supplied sources. The transcriptionist checks meaning and completeness before saving the production copy; physician signature and return routing are separate tasks.
tasks.previous_blocker: Producing varied medical and administrative materials requires transcription and formatting.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound transcription and document-type templates can reduce supported composition work.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve unclear dictation without inventing clinical content.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize ambiguity and preserve intended meaning.

ambition.what: Produce checked drafts with less mechanical transcription and formatting.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-8; authorized source processing and applicable staff consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: speech-to-text and source-bound drafting can assist production, with human fidelity checking.

assumptions: Boundary is producing supplied medical reports, correspondence, patient-care, statistical, research and administrative material, not independently performing research or clinical decisions.

Practitioners supply audio/source text, patient/encounter ID where relevant, requested type and intended purpose; existing analysts supply approved statistical tables with definitions and dates. s1 verifies these. Missing content is queried, not invented. No ambient recording is assumed.

Native dictation and templates come first. Central retains 35% of source transcription and 30% of formatting, with all final fidelity review retained. Numeric tables are deterministic and never generated from prose guesses.
Same-workspace save is effectively zero; minimum 1 is retained. Final production copy precedes approval and edits invalidate it.
Provisional B=100, R=60, gross=40; focal upkeep=2; net=38, independent of means priors.
research_questions: Compare drafts to original audio/text and time full correction including ambiguous medical terms.

already_counted.description: Verify final material meaning and source fidelity

incremental.description: Audit transcription omissions and maintain document-type templates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: existing transcription and templates already cover the proposed work. High: 40 gross points require ten extra correction hours and two upkeep hours, leaving 28.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify report mistakes and clarify facts with doctors

steps.what: Identify report mistakes by comparing the report with source material and terminology references
outputs: candidate report mistakes and ambiguous passages

steps.what: Frame the specific unresolved questions for the responsible doctor
inputs: candidate report mistakes and ambiguous passages

steps.what: Check with the doctor to obtain the correct information and resolve ambiguity
outputs: confirmed correction information and unresolved questions

steps.what: Record and verify the doctor's confirmed corrections and their source
inputs: confirmed correction information and unresolved questions

steps.what: Save the approved clarification record in the current report query

tasks.design: Configure terminology and field-consistency flags in {OTHER}, the transcription system, beside the source material. The transcriptionist still identifies semantic mistakes, asks the doctor precise questions and records the actual clarification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mechanical inconsistencies can consume source-comparison effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native terminology and identifier checks can flag a supported subset for review.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguish a transcription mistake from an unusual but intended clinical statement.
tasks.human_edge: Ask the doctor and preserve uncertainty until clarified.

ambition.what: Focus human checking on unresolved meaning.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: terminology and field-consistency checks can flag mechanical mistakes but cannot establish intended clinical facts.

assumptions: Boundary includes mistake identification, doctor clarification and recording confirmed information; later full report editing and signature are separate tasks.

Existing report/audio IDs, patient identifiers and approved terminology lists are inputs. s2 counts formulating the actual question and s4 counts capturing the doctor's actual answer, source, time and unresolved uncertainty. A rule flag never supplies a clinical correction.

Native checks come first. Central removes only 20% of identification effort through mechanical flags; questions, consultation and clarification entry remain unchanged. Existing checks eliminate additional savings.
Same-query save is effectively zero; minimum 1 is retained. Approval follows the completed clarification record and edits invalidate it.
Provisional B=100, R=91, gross=9; focal upkeep=0.5; net=8.5, independent of means priors.
unknowns: False flags and semantic error mix
research_questions: Compare flags with doctor-confirmed errors and count time spent dismissing false flags.

already_counted.description: Review flags and compare report meaning with sources

incremental.description: Maintain approved terminology and audit false flags

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: native checks are already used. High: nine hours of reduction face 2.5 extra false-flag hours and 0.5 upkeep hours, leaving six.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review and edit transcribed medical reports

steps.what: Review the transcribed report against the dictated source and intended report type
Check spelling, punctuation and approved medical terminology and apply verified mechanical corrections
Edit grammar, clarity, consistency and terminology meaning without changing clinical intent
Proofread the final edits against the source and approve the edited production copy
Save the approved edited copy in its current report workspace

tasks.design: Configure native spelling and approved-term suggestions in {OTHER} and {DOCS}. The transcriptionist checks each suggestion and retains full effort for grammar, clarity, consistency, clinical meaning and final source comparison.
tasks.previous_blocker: Mechanical spelling and terminology checks can interrupt substantive editing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native dictionaries and correction suggestions can assist the mechanical subset.
tasks.still_hard: An apparently fluent correction can alter medical meaning.
tasks.human_edge: Preserve the dictated intent and recognize ambiguous terminology.

ambition.what: Reduce mechanical checking while preserving substantive editing.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: spelling and terminology dictionaries can suggest corrections, while medical meaning requires source-aware human editing.

assumptions: Boundary is reviewing and editing an existing transcription, not creating initial transcription or returning it for physician signature.

Existing report/source IDs and an existing clinician-approved terminology list are required. Missing terms stay manual; no model expands an ambiguous abbreviation. Human checking and applying each accepted correction are retained in s2.

Native dictionaries come first. Central removes 60% of mechanical checking effort only; grammar and clarity edits remain fully human. If equivalent dictionaries are already used, there is no incremental saving.
Same-system save is effectively zero; minimum 1 is retained. Final proofreading precedes approval and changes invalidate it.
Provisional B=100, R=88, gross=12; focal upkeep=1; net=11, independent of means priors.
research_questions: Sample edits against original dictation and measure substantive versus mechanical editing effort.

already_counted.description: Check and apply accepted mechanical corrections
Verify final edited meaning against source

incremental.description: Maintain approved terms and audit harmful correction suggestions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: existing dictionaries already cover the mechanical subset. High: 12 gross points face three extra suggestion-check hours and one upkeep hour, leaving eight.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Transcriptionists retain source fidelity and doctor clarification; existing queues, dictionaries and bounded transcription assist supported production work.
reach: Physicians: resolve intended clinical facts and sign final reports
Record administrators: preserve exact report versions
skills_to_grow: Check negation and chronology against dictation
Distinguish mechanical corrections from clinical reinterpretation
Trace final signatures to corrected versions
role.ambitious_version: A transcriptionist who validates meaning and ambiguity while supported software handles repeatable transcription, formatting and review-copy routing.
